//: Install to /etc/org-request-mcp/config.json, owned by the operator user,
mode 0600. The server REFUSES to start on any mode with group or other
bits set — it holds a credential verifier and every company on this box
shares the host.
bearerSha256 is the SHA-256 of the shared bearer, NOT the bearer. Generate
the pair with:
bearer=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
printf '%s' "$bearer" | sha256sum          # -> bearerSha256, here
The bearer ITSELF goes to exactly two places, and something reads it in
both:
(a) Caddy's unit environment — this is what {$ORG_MCP_BEARER} in
Caddyfile.snippet expands from:
printf 'ORG_MCP_BEARER=%s\n' "$bearer" \
| sudo tee /etc/caddy/org-request-mcp.env >/dev/null
sudo chmod 600 /etc/caddy/org-request-mcp.env
sudo systemctl edit caddy   # EnvironmentFile=/etc/caddy/org-request-mcp.env
sudo systemctl restart caddy
(b) the Paperclip secret referenced by credentialRefs, for the gateway.
unset bearer
Nowhere else. An earlier draft of this file also had you write the bearer
to /etc/caddy/org-request-mcp.bearer. NOTHING ever read that file — the
Caddy snippet has always read the environment variable — so step 1 of the
install left a plaintext credential on disk serving no purpose (case_0409633c).
A read of THIS file does not yield a usable credential: it holds a digest.
capabilityScript (case_662081e3) is OPTIONAL. Set it to front capability_gate.sh
as well, exposing the three capability tools. Its basename is pinned to
capability_gate.sh at startup exactly as queueScript is pinned to
org_request_queue.sh. Leave it unset to front only the provisioning queue;
a capability tool called on a server without it fails CLOSED.
containerEngine (case_d8f38556) is OPTIONAL and defaults to podman. Set it to
docker on a Docker-only host such as node7b1ff338: the run corroborator and every
queue/capability invocation then use that binary (also handed to the
scripts as CONTAINER_ENGINE, alongside lib/pcsql.sh's PAPERCLIP_SQL_BACKEND
docker backend), instead of failing with missing podman.
